Insight · Build spec v0.2 · Developer handoff

One view of every organisation. One reason to act.

Insight is the intelligence layer inside Zoho CRM. It keeps one trusted record per nonprofit, connects signals to that record, scores fit and intent across six services, and gives the owner a traceable brief and a clear next action.

The product

What Insight must make possible.

The user should not have to assemble context from tabs, notes and spreadsheets. On an Account or Deal, they should immediately understand who the organisation is, why it matters now, which service fits, and what evidence supports the recommendation.

1canonical Account per organisation
6services scored independently
90minimum confidence for auto-match
70starting point for a Hot signal

Non-negotiables

Trust is part of the product.

These rules apply to every collector, field, score, brief and screen. They are not later compliance work; they shape the data model and the interface from the first build.

R1

State and history stay separate.

Accounts hold the latest state. Signals, interactions and money by year are rows that are never overwritten.

R2

Every enriched value is traceable.

Source, date and confidence travel with the value so a person can verify it.

R3

Uncertain matches wait for a person.

Below the confidence threshold, do not write to an Account until someone confirms.

R4

Public organisation data only.

No beneficiary or donor personal data. Redact personal data from conversation summaries.

R5

No Zolabs call content.

Zolabs recordings and transcripts stay outside Insight, in line with the AI usage policy.

R6

Permission wins.

Respect Email_Opt_Out and Communication_permission. Campaign data never overrides an unsubscribe.

R7

No unexplained scores.

Every score must show plain-language reasons. If reasons cannot be generated, do not show the score.

R8

Humans send.

Briefs and outreach drafts are suggestions. A person reviews them and decides what leaves the system.

System flow

Seven source families. One organisation.

Collectors save raw events first, then match, enrich and score. The design avoids copying mutable data into every Deal and preserves a complete history of what happened.

Identity gate

Sure matches write. Uncertain ones wait.

Compare Darpan ID, PAN, domain and normalised name. Confidence 90+ writes automatically; anything lower enters Match queue with evidence.

History rule

Accounts hold state. Events keep history.

Profiles may refresh, but signals, interactions and financial years remain immutable rows with source, date and confidence.

Human decision

The score explains; the owner decides.

Insight proposes a service, brief and next action. A person reviews the evidence before outreach or handover.

Core experience

Five screens define the first release.

These are functional specifications, not pixel-locked designs. The priority is the information hierarchy and the decision each screen helps a person make.

These are the full Zoho CRM references from the build boards. Select a screen, then click the image to inspect it at full size.

Signal inbox

A daily work queue that ranks what changed and gives the owner one action.

  • Tiles count today’s events, matched events, queue items and Hot signals.
  • Score is the highest service Intent_Score; hover or focus reveals the three reasons.
  • Below 90 match confidence, the row is amber and opens Match queue.
  • Account owner is default owner; unmatched signals remain unassigned.

Account Insight

The complete organisational context, embedded as a related-list tab on Accounts.

  • Header displays Completeness_Pct with Refresh and Write brief actions.
  • Brief is sourced, saved as a Note, and remains a draft until reviewed.
  • Six-service table reads Org × Vertical; signals are newest first.
  • Verified facts expose source and date; financials stay one row per year.

Deal workspace

The owner sees the recommendation at the moment a signal becomes an opportunity.

  • Keep the existing Internal CRM Flow; proposed later stages need confirmation.
  • Insight_Score and Insight_Reasons rewrite on every new signal.
  • Brief is also a Note and is explicitly marked Draft until reviewed.
  • Dismiss requires a reason and writes feedback to the Deal and Signal event.

Across services

A whitespace matrix of every organisation against the six ImpactOS services.

  • Build as a CRM canvas or custom view on Org × Vertical, grouped by Account.
  • Each cell is one service status; selecting it opens the underlying row.
  • Saved views turn cross-service rules into weekly work lists.
  • Campaign audience reads rolling Contacts.Engagement_Tier.

Match & sources

The operational control room for identity, source health and incomplete records.

  • Reviewer sees candidate evidence, not only a confidence number.
  • Confirm links the Signal event; Create makes an Account from raw identity.
  • Source failure turns amber and notifies the named feed owner.
  • Completeness queue shows Accounts below 50% with missing keys.
Data model

Eight modules around the Account.

The Account is the canonical, latest known profile. Every many-to-one satellite preserves a historical fact: an event, interaction, financial year, service relationship, match decision or source run.

Exists · extend

Accounts

Identity, registrations, profile, latest money, technology, best-fit service, highest intent, completeness and field-level provenance.

Exists · extend

Contacts

Work contact, role, communication permission, Campaign score, engagement tier and recent activity.

Exists · extend

Deals

Pipeline, stage, service, source signal, owner, amount, score, reasons, brief and next action.

New · history

Signal events

Type, source, detected date, strength, service tag, detail and match confidence. Append-only.

New · yearly

Org metrics

Income, expenses, programme spend, foreign funds, staff and beneficiary count by year.

New · history

Interactions

Email, meeting, call, voice note, webinar or reply; source-linked, redacted and outcome-tagged.

New · 6 per Account

Org × Vertical

Status, last touch, fit, intent, reason, open Deal and delivered Project for each service.

New · review

Match queue

Raw identity, candidate Accounts, evidence, decision, reviewer and date.

New · operations

Sources

Feed type, refresh rate, last run, status, terms review and records added.

Why separate modules?

An Account changes. A signal, a conversation or a year of income happens once and should stay as it was. Separating them prevents history from disappearing when the current profile is refreshed.

Signals and scoring

Fit changes slowly. Intent changes weekly.

Every organisation is scored independently for CRM, Data Systems, HRMS, Zolabs, ZolaShield and Custom AI. These starting weights must be tuned against real outcomes after launch.

One score, with evidence.

Fit comes from durable attributes: sector, size, geography, registration status and tools already in use.

Intent comes from events. Recent, strong signals count most and decay over time.

intent = Σ(weight × strength × decay)
decay halves every 45 days
scale result to 0–100

Show the three largest contributors in plain words. Example: “Posted a data officer role 12 days ago.”

Build order

Ship the identity spine first.

The phases deliberately make matching and traceability reliable before AI-generated briefs. Each phase has a visible definition of done and can be evaluated with real records.

Phase 1

Match and store

  • Store-signal match job
  • Match queue module
  • Sources module
  • Account provenance fields
  • Signal inbox
Done whenAlmost every Store signal links to an Account or sits in the queue with a reason.
Phase 2

Identity and money

  • Darpan, 12A, 80G, FCRA and CSR-1 fetcher
  • Org metrics module
  • Annual-report document reader
  • Completeness meter
Done whenEvery Account with a Darpan ID has dated, verified registrations and annual income where a report exists.
Phase 3

History and engagement

  • Interactions from approved history
  • Campaigns sync + service tags
  • Org × Vertical module
  • Across-services view
Done whenEvery Account has six service statuses and campaign clicks become service-tagged signals.
Phase 4

Score and brief

  • Fit and intent per service
  • Signal collectors
  • Sourced Deal brief
  • Account and Deal Insight tabs
  • Cadences and Deliver handover
Done whenAn owner opens a Deal and sees score, reasons and a reviewable brief without leaving CRM.
Current CRM baseline

Extend what already works.

AccountsRegistry fields exist and are fuller on older records. Tech stack fields exist but were empty in the sample.
Internal CRM FlowStore sign-ups already create Deals. At least 286 existed since 18 May, all at Signal Identified; roughly half linked to an Account.
LeadsZoho platform, users, data centre, customer status, credits, webinar attendance and Built for Impact are captured.
Native enrichmentLast Enriched Time and Enrich Status exist on Accounts, Leads and Contacts.
ScoringNo score fields appeared on Leads, Contacts or Deals through the API. Scoring rules may be switched off.
Deal layoutsInternal CRM Flow shows basic fields. Qualification fields currently sit on the Standard layout.
Still to inspectCadences, Campaigns sync, Notes content and Standard-pipeline history need an account-level check.
Before implementation

Six decisions need an owner.

The recommendations below let prototyping continue, but each should be explicitly confirmed before production automation is enabled.

01

What counts as a sure match?

Proposed: confidence 90 or above writes automatically; everything else waits for review.

02

Who owns the Match queue?

Name one person and a recurring weekly slot, or the queue will quietly become a backlog.

03

Which history may be read?

Confirm CRM Leads and Deals, Zoho Mail, meeting transcripts and voice notes individually, plus the redaction rule.

04

Is Campaigns sync enabled?

Need opens, clicks, unsubscribe and contact score, with one service tag on every campaign.

05

May each public source be automated?

Review terms and access constraints before any registry or website collector runs on schedule.

06

Are Cadences and scoring available?

Confirm plan availability. If Cadences are unavailable, move outreach steps to Campaigns.

Release-level acceptance

  • A raw signal is stored before any enrichment or scoring starts.
  • Every signal is linked to an Account or is visibly awaiting a decision.
  • No match below the agreed threshold writes to Account state.
  • Every enriched value exposes source, date and confidence.
  • Account state can update without deleting event or yearly history.
  • Every Account has exactly six Org × Vertical rows.
  • A score is hidden when no plain-language reasons exist.
  • Unsubscribed contacts never enter an outreach audience.
  • Generated briefs are clearly marked Draft until human review.
  • Dismissal and loss reasons feed back into future tuning.
  • Source failures surface to a named owner.
  • No beneficiary, donor or Zolabs call content enters Insight.
The build in one sentence

Make the right context impossible to miss.

Insight succeeds when an owner can open a Deal, trust what they see, understand why it matters, and choose the next action — without leaving Zoho CRM.
